meta.title: Hilbert Space Quantum Fest 2026
meta.description: Hilbert Space Quantum Fest 2026: five event days with lectures, lab sessions and a hackathon at Nazarbayev University in Astana. Free and open to everyone.
meta.cocTitle: Code of Conduct — Hilbert Space Quantum Fest 2026
meta.cocDescription: The code of conduct for Hilbert Space Quantum Fest 2026.

hero.lede: Five event days, lectures, lab sessions and a hackathon. Free of charge. No previous experience needed.

about.title: About the fest
body: Hilbert Space Quantum Fest brings together quantum technology enthusiasts to learn, explore and build projects together.

This year, it will happen in Astana, Kazakhstan for the first time. Dive into quantum computing, learn about its significant potential, and challenge your skills at the Hilbert Space Quantum Fest Hackathon.

whatYouGet.title: What you get
items: Lectures introducing quantum computing and quantum programming
Lab tours: Clean Room Nanofabrication & Cryo Superconducting Labs
A week-long hackathon where you can turn what you learn into working quantum computing projects

program.title: Program
program.subtitle: Read it as a quantum circuit — every week is a qubit, every session is a gate, and the hackathon is the measurement.

w1-cnot.title: Clean Room Nanofabrication & Cryo Superconducting Labs
w1-cnot.description: Laboratory session in the Clean Room Nanofabrication & Cryo Superconducting Labs.

hackathon.title: Hackathon
hackathon.lede: A week-long hackathon with 4 tasks and 1 optional project.

certificates.title: Certificates
certificates.lede: Two levels, both issued after the festival.
certificates.excellenceBody: At least four lectures attended, plus participation in the hackathon.
certificates.completionBody: At least three lectures attended, plus participation in the hackathon.

prerequisites.title: What you need
items: A basic level — we start from the ground up, no prior quantum background required

register.title: Register
register.lede: The fest is for university students, high-schoolers and independent researchers.
register.audience: University students, high-schoolers and independent researchers
register.note: The application takes about 3–5 minutes. Your answers are sent directly to the organizing team.

venue.title: Venue
venue.gettingThere: Details on entry and directions will be published together with the exact address.

items.q: I'm still in school — can I join?
items.a: Yes. The lectures start from the ground up and assume no university coursework. If you can follow along and you're curious, you belong here.

items.q: Do I need a background in physics?
items.a: Yes. To better understand the material: (a) review linear algebra on Khan Academy; (b) watch “A Beginner’s Guide to Quantum Computing” by Shohini Ghose on YouTube.

items.q: Do I need to know how to program?
items.a: A basic level helps. The Quantum Computing Lab on 14 November introduces quantum programming.
No. You can attend the lectures and lab tours without joining the hackathon.

items.q: What language are the lectures in?

items.a: You may participate individually or in a group of up to three people.

team.title: Team
trustBody: The same team runs National Science Battles — 1,800 participants across 7 countries — and the National Engineering & Science Olympiad — 600 participants across 3 countries.
Among us: a PhD student in quantum information at Oxford, graduates of quantum computing schools and research internships, and a NASA intern.

partners.title: Partners
partners.becomeBody: We offer logo placement, a slot to speak at the opening and closing, and coverage across social media and the press. You can support the festival with prizes or financially.

coc.title: Code of Conduct
coc.lede: Hilbert Space Quantum Fest 2026 is a learning space. Everyone is welcome, and everyone is responsible for keeping it that way.

sections.heading: What we expect
sections.body: Treat every participant, speaker, organizer and member of staff with respect. Assume good faith. Ask before you take someone's photo. Give people room to ask beginner questions — most of the room is a beginner at something.

sections.heading: What is not acceptable
sections.body: Harassment in any form, including comments about gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, disability, physical appearance, body size, race, ethnicity, religion or level of experience. Intimidation, stalking, unwelcome photography, sustained disruption of talks, and unwelcome physical contact or attention.

sections.heading: Academic honesty
sections.body: The hackathon is judged on what your team built. Use of libraries, published work and AI tools is fine when you say so. Passing off someone else's work as your own is not.

sections.heading: Consequences
sections.body: Organizers may take any action they consider appropriate, from a warning to removal from the event without a refund of any travel or costs, and exclusion from future events.

sections.heading: Reporting
sections.body: If you experience or witness a breach of this code, contact any organizer on site, or write to us. Reports are handled confidentially.
